body.label: Verso
body.value:
1. My life worsened further. She was arrogant to me through this boy of mine and the baby girl 

  2. that I maintained, with the poll tax that I had to pay. My livelihood in al-Maḥalla dwindled. 

  3. I became irritated (lit. my chest tightened) as my fortunes with women turned upside down. For I used to gaze at a wife (lit. a house) who had no equal 

  4. at all, whereas this kind of wife is unfit for a friend or an enemy.

  5. I entered the little one into a kuttāb because he is seven years old today. I do not have with me a 

  6. bible. Because of that reason I told you about, if you have something with you from 

  7. the days of the deceased, M(ay his) M(emory be blessed), that will show his (i.e. the writer’s seven year old son) favor with you, give it as a present to Abu’l-Hasan (i.e. the writerʼs son). For he is (like) your own son to the point that he 

  8. asks me for you and always says to me “my lord, show me my uncle!” I did not know 

  9. anything afflicted you until Abū’l-Surūr met me and told me what happened 

  10. to you with Yaḥya, the Elder, may he be remembered for his evil deeds by the divine law whose 

  11. power we all know. It saddened me, as whenever something is revealed about one of us, and especially you! May God, the exalted, punish him and may he not shame us by his reputation 

  12.  

  13. more than already took place. What happened to you with him will have no effect. Moreover, you will go 

  14. with him to the military commander, (let) someone else punish him! And now, my uncle, I do not 

  15. have any other pain that you (would) want to see, more than this matter. I am 

  16. in a state of fear regarding these people (i.e. the Ibn Sabra family) for I want to raise him and how will God help me 

  17. to be free from them? For they have made me grow old before my time! How I threw 

  18. myself down like a camel! I did not rush to Fustat to procure in it what I want, 

  19. instead, I have taken from the countryside the things I needed like “Harvest is past etc” (Jeremiah 8:20). I ask from 

  20. your kindness that you will not inform him of my situation nor where I am. For if it reaches (him), he will 

  21. attain shame among Jews. These people and I are in

  22.  such a situation! So strive to remove about me the wrong opinions. I also sent a letter to 

  23. inform my first in-laws that they should not inform him where I am. Send me (a letter) 

  24. informing me what happens with him, whether he is in the city or outside of it. Perhaps 

  25. he would encounter on the road what others encountered and we will not be picky. 

  26. In short, (tell me) everything that happens to him for he is my link to (what) I had in my previous life: he and his mother.

  27. with them (i.e. the Ibn Sabra family) are fifty dinars. They did not inform me of what is with them at all. Nor did they acknowledge to me 

  28. anything. While I carried them (on my expense) as if they were guests! The old 

  29. and the young treated them with honor out of respect to me. After that she joined him, obeyed him 

  30. and went behind him. A son of Israel buried her, may God attach her 

  31. to Him.

  2. who I maintained at my expense. (My) livelihood in al-Maḥalla dwindled.
  3. I became irritated (lit. my chest tightened) as my fortunes with women turned upside down. For I am looking at a house (meaning: a wife) who is completely not worth anything.
  4. For my house, in this shape, is unfit for a friend or an enemy.
  5. I entered the little one into a school (kuttāb) because he is seven years old today. I do not have with me
  6. a Bible (muṣḥaf). Because of the thing I told you about, if you have something with you that will show his (i.e. the writer’s 7-year-old son) favour with you 
  7. from the days of the deceased, M(ay his) M(emory be blessed), (give it) as a gift to Abū al-Ḥasan (i.e. the writer’s son). For he is (like) your own son to the point that he
  8. asks me for you and always says to me “my lord, show me my (paternal) uncle!” I did not know
  9. anything afflicted you until Abū al-Surūr met me and told me what happened
  10. to you with Yaḥyā, the Elder, may he be remembered for his evil deeds by the divine law whose
  11. power we all know. It saddened me, as whenever something is revealed about one of us,
  12. and especially you! May God, the exalted, punish him and may he not shame us by his reputation
  13. more than already took place. What happened to you with him will have no effect. Moreover, you will go with him
  14. to the military commander, (let) someone else punish him! And now, my uncle, I do not
  15. have any other pain that you (would) want to see, more than this matter. I am 
  16. in a state of fear with these people (i.e. the Ibn Sabra family) for I want to raise him and how will God help me
  17. to be free from them? For they have made me grow old before my time! How I threw
  18. myself down like a riding animal (for them)! I did not rush to Fustat to procure in it what I want,
  19. instead, I have taken from the countryside the things I needed like “Harvest is past etc”. I ask from
  20. your kindness that you will not inform him of my situation nor where I am; for if he will arrive
  21. at my location, there will be shame among Jews. These people and I are in
  22. such a situation! So strive to remove the suspicions about me. I also sent a letter
  23. to inform my first in-laws that they should not inform him where I am. Send me (a letter)
  24. informing me what happens with him, whether he is in the city or outside of it. Perhaps
  25. he would encounter on the road what others encountered and we will not be punctilious with him.
  26. In short, (tell me) everything that happens to him for he is my link to (what) I had in my previous life: he and his mother.
  27. With them (i.e. the Ibn Sabra family) are fifty dinars. They did not come to an agreement with me about what they have (of mine) at all. Nor did they acknowledge
  28. anything (i.e. any debt) to me. While I carried them (at my expense) as if they were guests! The old and the young treated them with honour
  29. out of respect to me. After that, she joined him, obeyed him and went
  30. behind him. She did not die with me. A son of Israel buried her, may God attach her to Him.

body.label: Verso
body.value:
פתנכר עיש֗י אכתר ואסתטאלת עלי בלולד אלדי לי ואלטפלה

  1. אלדי רזקתהא מע כון אלדי חצל לי כרג וקלת מעאישׁ פי אלמחלה   
  2. וצ֗אק צדי (!) כיף תעכסת פי נסאיה וכון אבצר בית מן לא יסוא   
  3. מגמל וביתי עלי הדה אלצורה לא יצלח לא לצדיק ולא לעדו וכאן  
  4. קד דכלת בלצגיר אלכתאב לאן עמרה אליום ז סנין ולם יכון ענדי 
  5. מצחף פלאגל הדא אלדי כלמתך אן יכון ענדך שי בין פצ֗לה ענך  
  6. מן איאם אלמרחום ז֗ל תהדיה לבואלחסן לאנה ולדך חתי אנה  
  7. יטלבך מני פי כל וקת יקול לי יא מולאי אוריני עמי ולם אעלם אנא 
  8. עררך איש֗ הו חתי אגתמע בי בואלסרור ואחכא לי מא גרי 
  9. עליך מן אלשיך יחיי יזכר במעש֗יו הרעים פי חק אלש֗רע אלדי  
  10. נעלם קדרה לקד גמי עלי כיף יכון מנא ואחד יצהר מנה דא  
  11. ובלכאץ פי חקך. פללה תעאלי יענשה ולא יכגלנא בסמעתה
  12. מצ֗אף אלי מא גרי ולקד מא גרי עליך מנה עגז בל כנת תדכל  
  13. מעה אלי צאחב אלחרב ישעף בה גירה ואלאן יא עמי אנא מא 
  14. כאן לי חרקה תשתהי אן תראה מצ֗אף אלי הדא אלפעל ואנא
  15. מע הולי אלקום עלי וגל לאני אריד אן ארבה וכיף יעינני אללה 
  16. עלי אלכלאץ מנהם לאנהם ש֗יבוני קבל חיני וכיף כוני רמית 
  17. רוחי מתל אלרכאב ומא נהצ֗ת אלי מצר לאנאל פיהא מא אריד 
  18. פלקד אכדת מן אלריף אלחאגה כמא עבר קציר וג֗ פאשתי מן 
  19. אנעאמך לא תטלעה עלי חאלי ולא אין אנא פאנה אן וצל 
  20. אלי ענד חצל בה בין ישראל כגל והולא אלקום ואנא תחת מתל 
  21. הדא אלחאל פאחרץ אן תבעד עני אלשבהה ואנפד אנא איצ֗א
  22. אעלם אצהארי אלאואיל אן לא יכברוה אין אנא ואנפת אנת
  23. אכברני איש כאן מנה אן כאן פי אלבלד או יכון כרג ולעל
  24. ילקא פי אלטרק מא לקי גירה ולא יכון לנא בה דקדוק ומן 
  25. גמלה מא גרי לה אנה וצלי אלי ענדי פי חיאה אלאולה הו ואמה
  26. ומעהם נִ דינאר מא אוקפוני עלי מא מעהם קט ולא קרו
  27. לי בש֗י וחמלתהם עלי כונהם ציוף כרמוהם אלכבאר
  28. ואלצגאר אכראם לי ובעד דא לחקתה וטאועתה ומצ֗ת
  29. כלפה ולם תמות ענדי אכפנהא בן ישראל פללה ילחקהא 
  30.                                                                       בה
